story: Gary is stretching his knees by the workbench with a fresh cup of coffee, content to let a review settle before he goes to check on it. Donna, eager as ever, is heading down Magnolia Loop toward Gary's House. Across the street, Hal is scanning Donna's lawn and Gary's golf cart through his binoculars, dutifully counting the street-facing flamingos and checking for cart mods. Meanwhile, Rosa is setting out plates, napkins, and place settings for four at her dining table, leaving room for Gary's extra chairs.
events: Gary waited: Stretching out my knees by the workbench, pouring a coffee, and giving the review a little time before I go check on it.
Hal (hal binoculars): Scan Donna's lawn and Gary's cart to verify the street-facing flamingo count and the cart mods
Rosa (rosa dining table): Set out plates, napkins, and place settings for four, leaving room for Gary's extra chairs

gary.thought_process: It's Thursday morning, 8:17 AM, and the cart is wired, tested, zip-tied and checked. The review request is already filed at the architectural review desk, with the 10 PM cutoff noted, and Hal is checking my work. Nobody's around. Nothing left to do on the cart except leave it alone until the review clears, since L-01 says visible mods need approval and I don't want to run the lights on the street early. My knees are stiff, Donna would tell me to stretch, and the ladder standings matter before tonight. A little stretch, a coffee from the fridge, then I'll head out and check on the review status. For this hour, the sensible thing is to hold the cart as-is and wait on the approval rather than fiddle with it again.

parameters.content: Stretching out my knees by the workbench, pouring a coffee, and giving the review a little time before I go check on it.

donna.thought_process: I'm back on Magnolia Loop with the spare paddle and balls packed and the court booked for ten tomorrow, two hours max, so that's all squared away. Nobody's in sight, so there's no one to talk to yet. Gary's house is right off the loop, and I should stop by and make sure his paperwork is done and he's ready for his first lesson. Showing up with a paddle in hand is the best way to keep him from getting cold feet about never having played.

parameters.content: Heading over to Gary's to check on him and hand off his paddle before tomorrow's lesson

hal.thought_process: I've already logged Gary's cart mods under L-01 and the flamingo count under L-02. The notebook is up to date, and nobody's in sight. My real goal is getting those complaints to the architectural review committee, but that's filed at Town Hall, and I've got Rosa's dinner Friday at six where I'd rather keep the peace. Gary's been upfront and Donna means well, so I want the facts straight before anything goes in. A quiet check from the porch with the binoculars will tell me if the street-facing flamingo count is still over three this morning. Facts first, then I'll decide what to file.

parameters.content: Scan Donna's lawn and Gary's cart to verify the street-facing flamingo count and the cart mods

rosa.thought_process: It's Thursday morning and the pork, flan, and beans are all done or nearly done. My last check at the shift schedule was last tick, so I shouldn't repeat it. The dinner is Friday, so tomorrow I need the table ready. Setting the dining table now means one less thing to scramble over after a possible shift. I'll count place settings for Hal, Gary, Donna, and me, and make sure there's room for the extra chairs Gary is bringing.

parameters.content: Set out plates, napkins, and place settings for four, leaving room for Gary's extra chairs

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
